messages:
lina-sales: Heads up - BetaCorp POC getting 403 on embeddings endpoint when calling from their backend. They say UI calls succeed, backend fails. Can SE take a look?

chris-se: Do we have the failing request sample and response body? 403 usually indicates permission/scopes or org/project binding mismatch.

lina-sales: Customer sent this: `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` Authorization: `Bearer sk.beta_789` Body: `{'input':'hello'}`. Response: `403 {"error":"permission_denied", "message":"scope_missing:embeddings"}`.

omar-eng: That message implies the key doesn't have embeddings scope. But you mentioned UI works? Could be they use a different key client-side (public demo key) or a proxy that swaps keys. Ask for the server env var and which key value they actually use.

sophia-support: Checking our logs for sk.beta_789... I see entries: `auth.check: token_kind=service_key, allowed_scopes=[generate], bound_to=org:org_beta`. So the key is generate-only. UI likely uses a different key with embeddings allowed.

chris-se: Two paths: 1) Give them a new service key with embeddings scope for server calls; 2) If they want a single key, update allowed_scopes to include embeddings. For security, prefer separate keys per surface (UI vs backend).

lina-sales: Customer asks about implications for Dedicated vs Hosted - they're on hosted trial. Any differences?

omar-eng: Hosted APIs accept both org and project bindings. For hosted, service keys can be org-bound. Their server should include header `X-Redwood-Org: org_beta` if using org-bound key, but scopes still control allowed endpoints. No header will result in auth failure if key requires it.

sophia-support: I generated sk.beta_temp_555 with scopes [embeddings, generate] and shared via secure channel to Lina. Also flagged that server must NOT expose keys in frontend.

lina-sales: Confirmed server now returns 200 using temp key. Customer asked: can we issue per-environment policy that blocks embedding-only keys from UI? They want guidance on best practices.

chris-se: Recommend: - Use short-lived client tokens for UI (public, limited scope) and service keys for backend. - Apply key binding to project/org as appropriate. - Enforce CORS + origin checks for any tokens returned by backend. - Create separate keys scoped narrowly, rotate keys regularly.

omar-eng: Also remind them to check proxies (e.g., serverless platforms) that might strip Authorization or swap headers. We saw a misconfigured CDN once that replaced Authorization header.

ci-bot: security-scan: note: sk.beta_temp_555 created at 1749991300 with scopes=embeddings,generate (ephemeral)

lina-sales: I'll send the temp key test confirmation and the best-practices checklist. Marking this resolved unless anything else?

chris-se: All good from SE. Recommend following up with a permanent key provisioning flow and confirm they rotate temp key after validation.

lina-sales: Thanks everyone :pray: Closing thread.
